newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act New Zealand launches 1996 election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Act New Zealand launches 1996 election campaign.

text.p: Richard Prebble, growing in confidence that his Act New Zealand Party would become a force in a new MMP parliament, launched the party's election campaign to a large and enthusiastic Auckland audience on Sunday.
"We are poised at the five percent threshold, but in-depth polling indicates that Act can get 21 percent of the vote," Prebble said.
The party leader, in a speech heavily pitched to "middle New Zealand", told cheering supporters that Act was all about personal freedom and responsibility.
Prebble also spent much of his addess covering Maori issues and the need to rid Maoridom of its social ills by Maoris taking control of their own destiny.
"The answer to the crisis in Maoridom is the same as it is for us all. Maori must take ownership of the problems. Maori must provide leadership and solutions."

He also reiterated the party's commitment to a flat tax rate, removal of Fringe Benefit Taxes on employer-sponsored health insurance, a compulsory pension scheme and retention and further development of an open market economy.

"Act is based on the core belief that at the heart of government should be Kiwi values - honesty, hard work, thrift, individual responsibility and inclusion," Prebble told a larger-than-expected turnout of about 1,200.

Act was formed two years ago by former Labour Government Finance Minister Sir Roger Douglas and former National parliamentarian Derek Quigley. From small beginnings, the party now had 14,000 members and 100,0000 supporters, Prebble said.
In a post MMP parliament, Act would not enter coalition deals but would act instead as a "broker" for sensible policy.
"The economy is one third larger than it was in 1986, Inflation is the lowest in my adult life," Prebble said.

"We have faster job growth than any country in Europe, a higher credit rating than Australia, and the Reserve Bank predicts that in 15 years we will be 50 percent wealthier than we are today," he said.
"Every social problem I've ever heard of will be eased by the country being that much wealthier."
Prebble said the policies of New Zealand First and the Labour parties were a worry to middle New Zealand and the leftist Alliance Party "scares the pants of middle New Zealand".
Successvie National and Labour governments had taken ordinary New Zealanders' votes for granted.
"Both parties have double taxed middle New Zealand to raise money so that they can bribe the floating voter."

A feature of the campaign was Act's push for the support of women -- nine of its top 20 list candidates are women. Prebble said he was confident Auckland lawyer Patricia Schnauer would take the seat of Tamaki. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
